name: The Machine Is Political
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Examine how technological systems allocate power, risk, and opportunity.

items.note: Three minutes presenting DAIR's report on Amazon delivery drivers: how workplace surveillance tech is used to cut pay and hide responsibility.
Mystery AI Hype Theater 3000, from DAIR's own instance, picks apart the claim that automation can strengthen democracy.
curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg at foss-north 2026 on what AI tools are really doing to open-source projects, from someone on the receiving end.
A talk on the Open Source AI Definition one year on: which 'open' models really are, and how to spot open-washing.
A CounterSpy conference talk from the Co-op Cloud project on platform surveillance and how cooperatives can run their own infrastructure instead.
A podcast episode with European Digital Rights on the trade-off between online safety laws and privacy, from the PublicSpaces coalition.
Waag Futurelab's yearly State of the Internet lecture, 2026 edition, given in English by Fieke Jansen with captions.
Rhizome's panel on the ethics of archiving digital folklore: memes, image macros, and who gets a say when the web's culture is preserved.
Members of the Kenya-based Data Labelers Association describe the human labor behind AI training data, and how they're organizing.
Nathan Proctor of the US PIRG on the right-to-repair fight and how copyright law (the DMCA) gets used to stop you fixing your own things.
Cory Doctorow's talk The Post-American Internet, posted with captions by Framasoft: an argument for interoperability as the way out of platform lock-in.
A LibrePlanet 2023 panel on why mainstream platforms are free of charge, what that costs the Global South, and what a libre alternative looks like.
Grant makers and builders debate who should fund technology that's given away for free, and which tech deserves public money.
A university seminar on digital governance frameworks for AI, from the team behind OpenFisca, the open-source rules-as-code engine.
A four-minute APC short on where digital rights and environmental justice meet, with captions.
New Design Congress on the 'para-real': how decentralised networks of care form when official systems fail people.
Artist Špela Petrič presents The Archive of In-Operables, made during a residency at Waag Futurelab: strange, thoughtful art at the edge of biology and tech.
